transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, it's nice to meet you too. I guess... what finally brought me in is that I feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people and, you know, take pleasure in my work, has gone very quiet. I'm a social worker, mostly dealing with mental health and substance abuse, which is a lot of reaching out, obviously. But lately, I'm mostly just moving through obligations. It’s like yoga, going to galleries, even my journaling—which I used to do every morning with this specific lavender tea I found at a little shop downtown. The owner there, she’s always so chatty, maybe a bit too chatty, but she has this incredible collection of vintage teapots... anyway, all of those things I used to enjoy, they just feel so distant now. I just do what I have to do and that's it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, let's see... this whole change in how I'm thinking, working, connecting with people, it's been going on for about eight months now. It started right around the time we took my older relative into our apartment. Which, honestly, was a whole ordeal in itself. Getting the apartment ready, I mean. We had to completely rearrange the guest room, and I ended up finding all these old photo albums in the closet while we were moving things around. There was this one picture of me from a trip to Sedona years ago—the red rocks there are just stunning at sunset, they look like they're practically glowing. I remember we stayed at this little bed and breakfast where they served the most amazing blueberry scones. I've tried to replicate the recipe a dozen times, but it never comes out quite right... but anyway, yeah, about eight months since she moved in.
Do you feel this started because of the stress of your older relative moving in with you?

I don't know... I'm not really sure if it was the stress, exactly. I mean, it’s a big adjustment, obviously, having another person in your space. She brought so many boxes with her, just endless stacks of them. We had to leave a few in the hallway for weeks. One of them actually had her mother's old Singer sewing machine in it. It's one of those heavy, cast-iron ones with the little gold painted decals on the side? It's really quite beautiful. I used to sew a bit, actually, back when I was getting my master's. I made these thick velvet drapes for my first apartment because the windows were terribly drafty. I remember going to this huge fabric warehouse on the east side to find the material, and the guy working there—he had this encyclopedic knowledge of textiles. He spent twenty minutes explaining to me how velvet originally used to only be woven from pure silk... but, um... what were we saying? Right, the stress. I just don't really know if that's what caused it.
Do you feel your low mood is mainly because of your older relative moving in with you?

I mean, like I said, I really couldn't tell you if she's the main reason. It's... I just don't know. We do have to share the kitchen a lot more now, and she insists on cooking almost everything from scratch. Which is fine, but she uses so much garlic, and the smell just completely lingers in the curtains. I actually tried buying this special neutralizing room spray online to deal with it. The reviews said it smelled like fresh linen, but honestly, it smells exactly like those little cardboard pine tree air fresheners people hang in their rearview mirrors? 

I had one of those in my very first car, this little powder blue Honda. I drove that thing all the way up to Chicago for a social work conference once. The highway was completely backed up for hours because a semi-truck carrying watermelons had tipped over on the shoulder. There were just smashed watermelons everywhere, all over the asphalt, and the smell of the sweet fruit baking in the hot sun was so overpowering... 

But, um... sorry, I lost my train of thought. You were asking about my mood? Yeah, I honestly just don't know if her moving in is the cause of it. I'm really not sure.
If your older relative moved out tomorrow, do you think you would still feel this same way?

I don't know... I really don't. It's hard to say what would happen if she just packed up and left tomorrow. Packing takes so much effort anyway. When we moved her in, we had to use those heavy-duty plastic bins instead of cardboard boxes because it was raining that whole weekend. It was one of those torrential downpours that just floods the streets in minutes. The drainage system on our street is terrible, it always backs up. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, actually had his entire basement flood last spring because of it. He had all these vintage comic books stored down there, completely ruined. He was devastated, of course. He spent years collecting them, going to all those little niche conventions... but, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. If she moved out. I just... I don't know if it would change how I'm feeling. I really couldn't tell you.
Before these past eight months, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt this same way?

I... I really don't think so. I can't remember ever feeling exactly like this before. I mean, everyone has periods where things are difficult, right? Like when I first started working as a social worker, right after grad school. That was a really intense time. I was assigned to this clinic downtown, and the commute alone was exhausting. I had to take the train, and it was always so packed. There was this one regular on my morning train, this older gentleman who always wore these brightly colored, patterned bow ties. Every single day, a different bow tie. I always wondered where he found them all. Maybe he made them himself? My aunt used to make her own clothes, actually. She had this incredible collection of vintage sewing patterns from the 1950s... 

Wait, sorry. What were you asking me? Oh, if I've felt this way before. No, I don't... I don't think I have. Not like this.
Do you feel hopeless?

Hopeless? Um... I don't know if I'd use that exact word. It's more just... I don't know. Words are tricky like that, aren't they? Like how people use the word "devastated" when they just mean they're a little disappointed they missed a TV show. My client last week, she told me she was absolutely devastated that the cafeteria ran out of those little chocolate pudding cups. They are good, though. They have that thick film on top? Some people hate that part, but I actually think it's the best part. It reminds me of the homemade pudding my grandmother used to make on Sundays. She had this heavy cast-iron pot she used for everything, from pudding to pot roast. You know, they say cooking in cast iron actually adds iron to your diet, which is so interesting. I read an article about it in a waiting room once... 

But, um... sorry. Hopeless. I just... I don't really know if I feel hopeless. I haven't really thought about it in those terms.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Down? Depressed? I... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling down most of the day. I mean, my days are pretty full, you know? Being a social worker keeps you busy, especially with the caseloads we have right now. It's just constant paperwork and phone calls. And the phones at the office are these really old, clunky models from like, the early 2000s. The buttons stick sometimes, especially the number four. I have a client whose phone number has three fours in it, and it always takes me twice as long to dial him because I have to press the button so hard. It's annoying, but what can you do? The agency budget is always so tight. They just cut the funding for our community outreach program, which is a real shame because we used to hand out these little canvas tote bags at events. People love a good tote bag. I have a whole collection of them hanging on the back of my bedroom door. I use this one from a farmer's market in Vermont all the time. It has a picture of a giant turnip on it... 

Um, but anyway. What was the question? Depressed? No, I... I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or down every day. Not really.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Concentrating? I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed any trouble with it. Not anything major, anyway. It's funny you ask about concentrating, though, because I was just thinking the other day about how hard it is to focus when there's a lot of background noise. Like at the office, the air conditioning unit right outside my window makes this constant, low hum. It's almost like a drone, you know? It reminds me of this documentary I watched last week about bees. Did you know that bees communicate through dancing? It's called a waggle dance. They literally do this little figure-eight movement to tell the other bees where the best flowers are. It's so fascinating how nature works like that. I used to want to be an entomologist when I was a little girl, actually. I had this whole collection of bugs I kept in glass jars in my room until my mom made me let them all go...

Wait, sorry. Concentrating. No, I don't think I've had any real trouble with that lately. I've been getting through my paperwork just fine.
Have you been sleeping more or less than usual lately?

Sleeping? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my sleep feels pretty normal, I guess. I usually try to get into bed by ten, but sometimes I stay up reading. I've been reading this really thick biography of Eleanor Roosevelt lately. She was such an incredible woman. Did you know she actually held her own press conferences where only female reporters were allowed to attend? It was her way of making sure newspapers kept women on staff during the Depression. It's brilliant, really, when you think about it. The way people had to get creative back then just to survive. Kind of like how people repurpose things now. I saw this video online of a woman who turned an old, beat-up piano into a bookshelf. She took all the keys out and painted the wood this lovely shade of teal. I love teal. My kitchen walls are painted teal, actually, and it makes the room look so bright in the morning when the sun comes through the window over the sink... 

Oh, right. Sleeping. Um, no, I haven't noticed sleeping any more or less than I usually do. It's been about the same.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Life not worth living? Oh, gosh, no. No, I haven't had thoughts like that. I mean, life is just so full, isn't it? There's always something going on. Even when things get stressful at work, I try to find the little things to appreciate. Like my garden. I started growing tomatoes this year, and let me tell you, there is nothing quite like the taste of a tomato you grew yourself. The ones at the grocery store are always so mealy and flavorless, you know? They pick them when they're still green and then spray them with gas to make them turn red. It's terrible. I read an article about it in this gardening magazine I subscribe to. The magazine is actually really great, they have all these tips for organic pest control. Last month they had a whole spread on using ladybugs to keep aphids away. You can actually buy ladybugs by the hundreds through the mail! Can you imagine the poor mail carrier delivering a box full of live ladybugs? I wonder if they can hear them buzzing in the package. My mail carrier is this really sweet guy named Frank. He always leaves a little dog treat for my neighbor's golden retriever...

But, um, what were we talking about? Thoughts about life? No, definitely not. I haven't been feeling that way at all.
Do you feel emotionally drained by your work?

Emotionally drained? Yeah, I guess you could say that. Actually, that's really what finally brought me in here. It's like... the part of me that used to reach out for people, or even just take pleasure in things, has gone very quiet. I'm a social worker, you know, and I used to get so much out of helping my clients, but now I'm mostly just moving through obligations. Same with my yoga, or going to galleries, or even journaling. I used to love journaling. I have this whole stack of Moleskine notebooks on my nightstand. The ones with the soft covers? They just feel so nice in your hands. I always buy the unlined ones because I like to sketch in the margins sometimes. I'm not a great artist or anything, mostly just doodles of plants and things. I tried to draw my sister's cat once, but it ended up looking more like a small bear. Her cat is huge, though. A Maine Coon. They get so big, it's almost like having a dog. And the fur gets everywhere! She has to vacuum her apartment every single day, which just sounds exhausting. I have a hard enough time keeping up with the dust in my place, especially with the construction going on down the street. They've been tearing up the road for weeks now, laying new pipes or something. The noise is just unbelievable in the mornings...

But, um, sorry. Work. Yeah, I just feel like I'm going through the motions with everything right now. The joy just isn't really there.
Has this been making it hard for you to do your job?

Hard to do my job? Well... I'm still showing up, you know? I haven't been calling out sick or anything. But I guess... yeah, it's been affecting things. I actually missed a couple of really big grant deadlines recently. Grants are so tedious, anyway, with all the paperwork and the specific formatting they want. You have to use exactly the right font size or they'll just throw your application out without even reading it. It's ridiculous. My friend Sarah works in grant writing for an arts non-profit, and she says they spend half their time just arguing over margins. She's the one who got me into those Moleskine notebooks I was telling you about. We used to go to this little stationary shop downtown on our lunch breaks. It's closed now, though. The owner retired and moved to Florida. A lot of people seem to move to Florida when they retire. I don't think I could handle the humidity down there. My hair gets so frizzy just when it rains here, I can't imagine what it would do in a swamp. I tried using this anti-frizz serum once, but it just made my hair look greasy... 

Oh, right, my job. Um... yeah, so I missed those deadlines. And my supervisor, she's been really quiet about it, but I noticed she's been moving some of my more demanding clients over to other clinicians. I think she knows I'm just... not functioning at my usual level right now.
Outside of work, do you still enjoy the things you used to enjoy?

Enjoy things outside of work? Um... no, not really. Like I said before, I just don't have the energy for it. Even things I used to look forward to, like my yoga classes. I haven't been to the studio in weeks. It's a shame, too, because I really liked my instructor. Her name is Chloe, and she always plays the most relaxing music during the cool-down part at the end. Lots of acoustic guitar and singing bowls. Have you ever heard a singing bowl? They make this incredible vibrating sound that you can actually feel in your chest. My aunt bought one when she went on a retreat in Sedona a few years ago. She's really into all that new-age stuff now. Crystals, aura readings, the whole nine yards. She even tried to get me to go to an astrologer once to figure out why I was having trouble sleeping. I told her I'd rather just drink some chamomile tea. I love tea, especially in the winter. I have this whole collection of loose-leaf teas in my pantry. There's this one Earl Grey blend that has little dried lavender flowers mixed in... 

But, uh, no. I'm just not finding much joy in anything right now. It's all just kind of flat.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

Tired? Um... I don't know if I'd say unusually tired. I mean, I'm always kind of tired, but I haven't really noticed a big change or anything. It's not like I'm falling asleep at my desk. Though, honestly, my desk chair is so uncomfortable I don't think anyone could sleep in it. It's one of those ergonomic ones that's supposed to be good for your posture, but it just digs into my lower back. I tried bringing in a little lumbar pillow, this cute blue one with a geometric pattern, but it didn't really help. I got it at Target, actually. Target has such good home stuff lately. Have you seen their new spring collection? Lots of bright colors and woven textures. I almost bought a new throw blanket for my couch, but then I remembered I already have three. My cat, Barnaby, loves sleeping on the softest one. He kneads it with his paws for like ten minutes before he finally settles down. It's adorable, but he ends up pulling the threads out. He's a rescue, you know. Found him in an alley behind my old apartment building...

But, um, energy. No, I don't think my energy levels are any lower than usual. Just the normal amount of tired, I guess.
For most of the past eight months, have you felt this loss of interest and going-through-the-motions feeling on most days?

Most days? Yeah... I mean, this whole change in how I'm thinking and working, and just, you know, connecting with people... it's been going on for about eight months now. It started right around the time we took my older relative into our apartment. Which, let me tell you, was a huge adjustment. We had to completely rearrange the guest room to fit her hospital bed. And those beds are incredibly heavy. The delivery guys scratched the hardwood floor in the hallway bringing it in. It's a shame, too, because we just had those floors refinished last year. We went with this really nice dark walnut stain. It looks beautiful, but it shows every speck of dust. I feel like I'm constantly running the Swiffer over it. I buy those dry sweeping cloths in bulk at Costco now. Costco is amazing, isn't it? You go in for one thing and come out with a giant tub of pretzels and a kayak. My husband actually bought a kayak there once. He thought he was going to take it out on the lake every weekend, but it's just been sitting in the garage collecting dust... 

But, um, yeah, the timeline. About eight months of just feeling like I'm going through the motions, pretty much every day.
Have you been feeling worthless or like you're letting people down?

Worthless? Um... no, I wouldn't say I feel worthless. I don't really think I'm letting anyone down, either. I mean, I still do my job and everything. Being a social worker, you know, people rely on you. You can't just drop the ball. Though, honestly, sometimes I wonder if the system itself is dropping the ball. The paperwork alone is just... it's a mountain. I was trying to organize my files the other day, and I found this old folder from like three years ago. It had all these colorful tabs I made with my label maker. I love my label maker. It's one of those old-school ones where you punch the letters in and it makes that satisfying clicking sound. I used it to label all the spices in my kitchen, too. My husband thought I was crazy, but it looks so neat. We have this big spice rack that spins, like a lazy Susan. It's really convenient, except when you spin it too fast and the little jars fly off. We lost a whole jar of smoked paprika that way. Red powder everywhere. It took me forever to get it out of the grout on the kitchen counter...

But, uh, no. I don't feel worthless or like a burden or anything like that. Just... you know, flat.
Have you noticed your appetite changing lately?

Appetite? Um, no, not really. I think I'm eating about the same as I always do. I usually just have a piece of toast for breakfast. Sometimes with that natural peanut butter, you know, the kind where the oil separates at the top and you have to stir it for like five minutes before you can actually use it? It's such a hassle. I tried storing the jar upside down because someone on the internet said that prevents the separation, but it didn't really work. It just made the lid all greasy. I hate when jars get greasy on the outside. It reminds me of this Italian restaurant my husband and I used to go to for our anniversary. They had these little cruets of olive oil on the table that were always so slick you could barely hold them. The food was amazing, though. They had this butternut squash ravioli with a sage butter sauce that was just... out of this world. Sadly, they closed down during the pandemic. A lot of places in our neighborhood did. It's really changed the vibe of the street. There's a new boutique there now that sells, like, artisanal candles for fifty dollars. Who pays fifty dollars for a candle? I mean, I like a nice scent, but I usually just get mine at Bath and Body Works when they have their semi-annual sale... 

But, um, anyway, my appetite. No, it hasn't changed. I'm eating normally, I think.
During these past eight months, was there any stretch of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

A stretch of two months? Um... no, I don't think so. It's just been pretty continuous. Two months feels like a really long time right now. It's almost a whole season, you know? Like, summer just completely flew by this year. We didn't even get to go to the beach. We usually rent this little cottage down in Cape May for a week in August. It's nothing fancy, just a tiny two-bedroom place with an outdoor shower, but it's right near the boardwalk. I love walking on the boardwalk in the early morning before it gets too crowded. The seagulls there are absolutely ruthless, though. I saw one swoop down and steal a whole slice of pizza right out of a teenager's hand once. Just swooped, grabbed it, and flew off. I usually just get the boardwalk fries anyway. You know the ones that come in a big paper cup and you just drown them in malt vinegar? They are so bad for you, but they taste amazing. I tried making them at home in the air fryer, but it’s just not the same. Everybody says air fryers are this miracle appliance, but honestly, mine just takes up half the counter space and is impossible to clean... 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling back to my usual self. No, there hasn't been any break like that. Just the same going-through-the-motions feeling the whole time.
Has this been causing you significant distress?

Distress? Um, I don't know if distress is the right word. It's frustrating, I guess. I mean, I'm still showing up to work every day, but I know I'm not functioning at my usual level. Like, I've missed a couple of big grant deadlines recently, which really isn't like me at all. And my supervisor has quietly started moving some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. 

She’s really sweet about it, actually. Her name is Brenda, and she always wears these huge, beautiful turquoise necklaces. She told me she gets them from this little artisan market in Santa Fe when she visits her sister out there. I’ve always wanted to go to New Mexico. The desert just seems so peaceful, you know? All those red rocks and the open sky. I actually bought a little cactus for my desk recently, thinking it would bring a little bit of that Southwestern vibe into my office, but I think I overwatered it. It just turned to total mush at the base. You'd think a cactus would be the one plant that's impossible to kill, but apparently, they hate having wet feet. That's what the guy at the garden center called it—'wet feet.' It's such a funny expression for a plant. I ended up having to throw the whole pot away because the soil started smelling like a swamp, and you can't really have that kind of smell in a social work office... 

But, um, anyway. Yeah. I'm just not at my usual level right now, so they're shifting things around for me.

patient.answer:
I mean, like I said, I really couldn't tell you if she's the main reason. It's... I just don't know. We do have to share the kitchen a lot more now, and she insists on cooking almost everything from scratch. Which is fine, but she uses so much garlic, and the smell just completely lingers in the curtains. I actually tried buying this special neutralizing room spray online to deal with it. The reviews said it smelled like fresh linen, but honestly, it smells exactly like those little cardboard pine tree air fresheners people hang in their rearview mirrors?
